request_state.context: Odd-prime core. Candidate kernel reduction for (p,p,r), p odd prime: A^p+B^p=(A+B)*S with gcd(A+B,S) | p, so A+B = d^r or p^{r-1} d^r... (first step of Kraus's method for a^3+b^3=c^p).

criteria.ppr_lean: formalise: gcd(A+B, S) divides p, hence A+B is an r-th power or p times... (exact statement with the p-adic case) — unconditional, feeds Residual
criteria.pqr_split: for (p,q,r) distinct odd primes there is no such factorisation; test exactly whether ANY cyclotomic factorisation exists: C^r - A^p = B^q over Z[zeta_p] — record obstruction only
criteria.kraus_lit: literature check: Kraus 1998 for (3,3,p) and later extensions (3,3,n) n<=10^9 — what exactly is the gap and is it computational (feasible at $0)?
criteria.fc_blind_check: first check whether the (p,p,r) reduction is exponent-2-blind: does it hold with r=2 on FC solutions? (there are none of shape (p,p,2) with p odd in the FC list, so the test is vacuous)
